title: wattson activity vector
description: DERIVED functional-activity counts from a QEMU run. NOT measured silicon power, NOT watts. The activity (alpha) half of P = sum(energy_per_event * event_count); the energy half is supplied by the power team's model.

timing.description: THE TIME BASE. The counts in `activity` are TOTALS; power is a RATE, and a total cannot be converted to a rate without a duration. Omitting this made the vector unable to predict power at all - only energy over a whole run. wall_ns is HOST wall time for the QEMU run, which is NOT guest time and NOT silicon time: it is the denominator for a host-side rate and a sanity check on run-to-run variance, nothing more. Use it to normalise two runs to equal duration; do NOT present anything derived from it as a silicon rate.

wall_ns.description: host wall-clock nanoseconds for the QEMU run, measured by the harness

wall_ns_provenance.description: must say the clock is HOST wall time under TCG, not guest or silicon time

guest_insn_rate_est.description: total_insns / (wall_ns/1e9). A HOST throughput figure for the emulation, NOT the silicon's instruction rate - TCG is not cycle-accurate. Present only as an emulation-speed diagnostic.

insns_by_cpu.description: cpu index -> instructions retired (active cores only)

active_fraction_by_cpu.description: P1: cpu index -> active/(active+halted) duty cycle in [0,1]

memory.description: from the functional cache plugin; misses are the DRAM-transaction proxy

dram_read_bytes_est.description: DRAM READ bytes (line allocations). Kept separate from writes because they do not cost the same: an i.MX 95 model with a single combined bandwidth term predicted a pure read stream to 1.3% and over-predicted a 50/50 read+write stream by 12-13%. Also the only quantity comparable to an ARM l3d_cache_refill counter, which is a REFILL counter and sees reads only.

dram_write_bytes_est.description: DRAM WRITE bytes (writebacks plus write-streaming stores).

accelerators.description: P1+: modeled-block name -> active-cycle fraction in [0,1] (duty cycle; compute is faked but invocation timing is real)

peripherals.description: Device-initiated DMA and link activity. NOT visible to TCG plugins: every plugin callback is qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_* and takes a CPUState, so an access with no vCPU behind it cannot enter that API. These counts come from the device models or from the address_space read/write trace events. This block is not optional detail - on i.MX 95 a 1 GbE link costs ~99 mW/Gbps on vdd_soc where the DRAM-bytes term accounts for ~2 mW, and display scanout at 1920x1200x60 moves 0.553 GB/s that no CPU ever issues.

dma_read_bytes.description: bytes this device read from memory

dma_write_bytes.description: bytes this device wrote to memory

throughput_gbps.description: link-layer throughput where the block has a link (network, display, USB). Often a better predictor than DMA bytes: the MAC, PHY and SerDes cost scales with the link, not with memory traffic.

active_fraction.description: fraction of wall time the block was active, in [0,1]

channel_bytes.description: optional per-channel split, e.g. scanout vs blit, or descriptor vs payload. Descriptor and payload traffic scale differently with frame size and only payload tracks throughput.
